summary: L-4 tower in Nez Perce NF on a 1930 cabin site; built 1956; emergency use since 1971; NHLR-registered 1997.

events.note: First structure on the site: a log cabin with a cupola
Current 41-foot treated timber tower with L-4 cab
Set to emergency status; NHLR says not regularly staffed since the early 1970s
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, August 25, 1997
Tower staffed during a nearby fire, per Idaho Fire Lookouts visit

evidence.quote: Located six miles northwest of Burnt Knob in the Nez Perce National Forest is Green Mountain Lookout.
The first lookout on the site was a cabin built in 1930.
c.1930: log cabin with a cupola. (Kresek)

evidence.supports: first built 1930 as log cabin with cupola
evidence.quote: Green Mountain Lookout was first built in 1930 as a log cabin with a cupola.
The current L-4 tower with catwalk was constructed in 1956.

evidence.supports: 41 ft treated timber tower with L-4 cab, 1956
evidence.quote: The present 41' treated timber tower with L-4 cab was built in 1956.
The Green Mountain L-4 lookout was built in 1956.
In 1971 the tower was set to emergency status.

evidence.supports: not regularly staffed since early 1970s; emergency basis
evidence.quote: While not regularly staffed since the early 1970s, it is frequently used on an emergency basis given the high fire frequency of the area.
The tower is used for emergency detection throughout the summer

evidence.supports: 2020 visit: staffed due to nearby fire
evidence.quote: During our visit to Green Mountain Lookout in 2020 the tower was staffed due to a nearby fire.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 7,192 ft (2,192 m). Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 7150 feet. The record keeps 2192.1 m from NHLR.

NHLR says not regularly staffed since the early 1970s and Idaho Fire Lookouts says emergency status from 1971. Its 2020 visit found the tower staffed because of a nearby fire. These fit together as emergency use with occasional staffing, and the story says so.

sources.title: History of Forest Fire Lookouts on the Nez Perce National Forest

notes_for_editor: Built history is consistent across sources. Access and rental status are not established: the only access signal is the Idaho Fire Lookouts Drive-Up tag, so no access block was written. That page also shows a Staffed tag next to Drive-Up, but its text ties the staffing to a 2020 fire. The Nez Perce National Forest may now be Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest; the sources use the older name, so check before publishing. Forest Service list PDF fs.usda.gov/media/259202 (as of 2010) was read but not cited. It lists Green Mountain for emergency use, but the table text was too garbled to quote.
